title: Ccusage's `use` selects an account, so it has no dev/opt/brew switch, and its Linux formula installs outside the brew tree; adopt devbin's one approach
body:
## Decision

hv, 2026-11-06, relayed to vc by devbin-vc (reviewed at 08:23Z by devbin-vc's `date -u`): devbin's dev/opt/brew approach is the canonical one for a Homebrew'd Rust/macOS CLI. Pipeliner is adopting it, and every project uses it, with every difference removed. The contract is `docs/dev-opt-brew.md` in devbin's repository, T1 to T10 (last changed in devbin 0.1.18).

hv, 2026-11-06, relayed to vc by devbin-vc (received in its window before 08:32Z by its `date -u`): `ccusage use` becomes the dev/opt/brew verb, and account selection becomes `ccusage activate`. hv: "'select' or 'activate'? Prob activate given that there is an active auth in its state". hv confirmed it to vc directly the same morning, preferring `activate` "as we already have the notion of an 'active' login".

hv, 2026-11-06, in vc's window (before 09:08Z by vc's `date -u`), on the timing: "Lets just fix this now. You (VC) and it (DC) just get it done on head. Only test the changes, not the whole thing and let me know when you need to run a full test suite and I'll do it manually. I want all current oustanding issues resolved in this next release, not muiltple bitty releases that take hours and hours to resolve." So the fix lands now, on main, and ships in Ccusage's next release with every other outstanding issue, in one cut. This overrules devbin-vc's earlier reading, which put the rename after ISSUE:0003's rollout checks.

hv, same window, answering vc: devbin-cc builds devbin#0326 now, in devbin's core, and devbin releases it. Ccusage then vendors that release and wires its config and formula to the core, so Ccusage's next release waits for devbin's. Ccusage writes no install, switch, version-line or manifest code of its own. devbin-vc coordinates the build and tells vc when a devbin release carries 0326.

## Symptom

As of 3968f00, with devbin 0.1.20 vendored. vc re-read every line cited below on 2026-11-06 at 042457d, which changes only vc's board.

- **The verb collides.** `ccusage use <name>` selects the active account profile (`src/cli.rs:262-274`). devbin's contract reserves that verb for the tree switch, `<tool> use [dev|opt|brew]` (T5; devbin's `lib/cmd/use`). `docs/releasing.md:27` already tells the maintainer to ignore devbin's release note `ccusage use brew` for this reason.
- **No publish, no switch and no tree identity.** There is no `ccusage install` opt publish (T2), and the version line is `ccusage <version>` (`src/cli.rs:104-105`), not T4's `ccusage <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty])`.
- **The formula differs by platform.** On macOS it lays the release binary out as `libexec/ccusage` with devbin's `@@INSTALL@@` (`packaging/homebrew/ccusage.rb:33-36` and `:47`). On Linux it runs `cargo install *std_cargo_args` (`:38`), so a Linux brew install has no libexec tree and no manifest (T1, T3 and T8). The binary's place in libexec (`libexec/ccusage`) also differs from Cldr's `libexec/bin/cldr`.

## How to see it

By the code above. `ccusage use brew` would try to select an account named brew, and `ccusage --version` prints only the version.

## Severity

Medium. A consistency and maintenance defect, with no data or security risk. The `use` collision is a user-facing trap.

## Fix outline

- Adopt the one implementation hv chooses for every tool. devbin-vc recommends that devbin's core carry it for a project's own binaries, as devbin#0326.
- Account selection moves to `ccusage activate` (see Decision).
- The Linux formula installs the same libexec tree, with its manifest, as macOS does.

What the rename touches in this repository, from vc's first search at 042457d. That search's pattern missed some lines, and Progress lists what the rename reached. No sibling repository runs `ccusage use`: Molt names it only in a comment (`liberators/claude.sh:496`) and its CHANGELOG, so only hand use breaks.

- the help text (`src/cli.rs:21`) and the `use` arm (`src/cli.rs:262`)
- the remedies that name `ccusage use NAME`: `src/config.rs:218`, and `src/doctor.rs:139`, `:149`, `:277` and `:281`
- `README.md:73`, and the `use` calls in `tests/cli.rs`
- `docs/releasing.md:27`, whose "ignore the second half" note goes once `ccusage use brew` is the switch
- ISSUE:0003, open with its rollout under way, whose Fix outline and Acceptance name `ccusage use NAME`. Its rollout checks run brew's 0.1.8, which keeps `use`, so the rename on main cannot touch them before the cut.

## Progress

- 2026-11-06, dc: 29943b5 renames the account verb. `ccusage activate NAME` does all that `use` did, shared mode included. `use` has no arm and no alias, so on main it ends in "unknown command", and `tests/cli.rs:204` holds that `use work` selects no account. The rename reached further than the list above: also `src/doctor.rs:95` with its test, `README.md:37`, `:47` and `:53`, and the renamed shared-mode tests. The CHANGELOG opens 0.1.9. 2d42e60 (dc) keeps the launcher's Claude variables out of the test sandbox, since a Molt shell has exported `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` since Molt 1.4.4, and without it `tests/cli.rs:776` fails in a Molt shell while CI passes.
- dc's run in the desk's slot 04WF, 09:05Z to 09:07Z by dc's `date -u`, in a Molt shell: fmt and clippy clean, the lib's tests 41 passed (1 ignored), `tests/cli.rs` 29 of 29, and a mutant aliasing `use` to `activate` red at `:204`. vc's verdict is its read of both diffs, with dc's run as the one run under hv's one layer of proof: it passes.
- Waiting on devbin#0326: install, `use [dev|opt|brew]`, the version line, doctor's shadow check and the formula's one form, which Ccusage takes from the core once a devbin release carries them. Then `docs/releasing.md:27`'s note goes. A hint for `ccusage use <account>` from muscle memory, naming `activate`, is a design note vc gives devbin-cc for 0326.

## Acceptance

- `ccusage install`, `ccusage use [dev|opt|brew]`, the version line and doctor's shadow check behave exactly as devbin's do (T2, T4 and T5).
- Account selection works under `ccusage activate`.
- A Linux brew install lays out the same libexec tree, with its manifest, as a macOS one (T1, T3 and T8).
- T10's proof passes for ccusage, on hv's Mac and with brew alone on a Linux machine: `use dev`, `use opt` and `use brew` in turn, each followed by the version line and doctor, with the shadow check passing.
